text: A garment factory in Bangladesh, thirty days before a buyer audit. Its fire safety certificate expires before the auditor arrives, and the proof sits in scattered P D Fs.
This is ThreadLight, running live on our server. We sign in to the real A P I as the compliance officer. All data is synthetic.
The passport comes from the database: coverage is 29 percent, and the risk index is 63. The fire certificate expires before the audit.
Now we upload a real P D F: the renewed fire certificate, replacing D 1.

The pipeline runs live. It reads the text, hides personal data, classifies the document, and Gemini extracts the fields, each with a quote and page number. Every field is checked against the page. Then it is indexed for search, and the rules engine runs again. Fast forward.
The document now waits for a person. The officer sees exactly what was extracted, and approves it. The A I can never approve or close anything.
After approval, the rules re-run: the fire safety requirements are supported, and coverage rises from 29 to 55 percent.

Under the hood: OCR for scans and Bangla, Gemini for extraction and bilingual drafts, hybrid search with pgvector, a LangGraph pipeline with human approval steps, and an MCP server for buyers and auditors. Every model call is logged, and the evaluation results are shown here.
Models read. Rules decide. People approve. Models only extract cited fields and draft text; deterministic rules decide every status; and a named person approves the evidence.
The result: fewer audit surprises, and fixes you can prove. Next, a pilot with export factories on real documents. ThreadLight: evidence you can verify, before the auditor asks.
